dimension_justifications.soundness: The storage-range predicates, factorial relations, selected FP32/NumPy sidecars, and matched mutants are coherently specified. However, the central evidence is conditional on author-produced capture records, selected operator boundaries, and an unbound compiled dispatch path; it cannot independently establish runtime behavior or rule out broad common-mode failures.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper is unusually explicit about scopes, denominators, and non-claims, with readable figures and tables. It is nevertheless very dense and repetitive, and its many cohorts, qualifications, and appendix tables make the main contribution harder to isolate than necessary.
dimension_justifications.contribution: A receipt-oriented integration of lifecycle, ownership, call, and accounting records for hybrid KV/GDN state is a useful systems-testing perspective. The paper itself establishes that constituent ideas are prior art (Appendix G), while validation remains tied to one customized sequential stack, limiting demonstrated novelty and broader significance.

paper_summary: ForkAudit is a receipt-bound audit contract for request isolation in a hybrid attention/GDN LLM stack. It evaluates four KV-by-GDN ownership configurations on one frozen Qwen3.5-35B-A3B setup, reporting equal registered outputs/state across cells, selected attention and GDN numerical checks, targeted fault gates, and explicitly separated memory accounting; auxiliary serving and related-work cohorts are kept unpooled.
strongest_verified_contribution: Within the paper-visible frozen setup, the strongest result is a carefully bounded receipt-replay protocol that reports matching registered token, full-logit digest, logical-KV digest, and final-GDN digest observations across 96 four-cell factor configurations and 288 adjacent-fan-out comparisons (Section 5.3, p. 8), together with explicit storage-lifecycle predicates (Sections 3-4, pp. 3-5).
strengths: Claim boundaries are unusually responsible: the abstract, Sections 5-6, and Appendix I explicitly exclude independent recapture, end-to-end verification, concurrent kernels, capacity, and broad performance conclusions.
The contract distinguishes immutable token-indexed KV from recurrent state and states concrete setup, first-transition, and final-phase ownership obligations (Section 3, pp. 3-4).

The evaluation separates relational equality, selected independent numerical checks, and targeted positive controls rather than presenting them as equivalent evidence (Figure 3 and Sections 5.3-5.5, pp. 8-9).
Memory reporting separates logical/pool accounting from allocator counters and avoids interpreting them as NVML capacity (Section 4.4, p. 5; Tables 6 and 16, pp. 16 and 21).
PDF-visible citations are consistently linked to a bibliography, and the novelty table candidly positions the work relative to prior systems and testing methods (Appendix G, pp. 18-19).
questions: Can the authors provide an independently instrumented capture or an independently implemented execution path that validates ownership receipts rather than merely replays producer-captured records?

How does the contract behave under actual concurrent CUDA kernels, ragged/continuous batching, multi-document prefix sharing, eviction, and scheduler decisions, rather than deterministic one-stream request steps?
Why should the proposed integration be considered a sufficiently new research contribution beyond a carefully engineered test/audit harness, given the prior-art decomposition in Tables 9-10?
Can a reduced end-to-end independently computed reference establish semantic correctness across all hybrid layers, not only eight attention rows and four post-normalization GDN transitions?

issues.location: Section 3, pp. 3-4; Section 4.3, p. 5; Table 5, p. 15; Appendix I, p. 23
issues.observed_evidence: The decision rule labels targets "full" when receipt fields replay, but explicitly conditions this on "honest capture" and external byte bindings; Section 4.3 says replay cannot reconstruct unarchived device tensors or independently recapture the producer. Appendix I likewise states that pointer-free intervals and hashes are not protection against a malicious producer before capture.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's central ownership conclusion is therefore evidence about a captured ledger, not independent evidence that the runtime actually owned and mutated the claimed device state. This is a legitimate caveat, but it materially constrains the scientific force and portability of the main result.
issues.required_fix: Add an independently instrumented capture/verification path, or a separately implemented runtime/reference that derives and checks ownership observations without reusing the producer's capture machinery. Archive sufficient sampled raw state to audit the binding from runtime state to receipts.
issues.verification_test: A blinded verifier using independently produced traces should reproduce the lifecycle/disjointness outcomes and identify injected aliases without consuming producer-generated storage-role records as ground truth.
issues.evidence_needed: Independent trace captures, raw sampled tensor/page data with provenance, and agreement/disagreement analysis between the independent and original capture paths.

issues.location: Sections 4.1-4.3, pp. 5-6; Section 6, p. 9; Appendix I, p. 23
issues.observed_evidence: The primary factorial uses one model, one H20 family, N in {1,8,32}, one partial-tail geometry, batch size one, and sequential round-major steps on one CUDA stream. The paper expressly excludes concurrent kernels, continuous/ragged batching, eviction, multi-document serving, admission capacity, and production scheduling.
issues.why_it_matters: The motivating use cases are serving forks, agents, and tree search, where concurrency and scheduler behavior are central to both ownership bugs and memory accounting. The current experiment demonstrates a narrow adapter-specific lifecycle audit, not practical serving robustness.
issues.required_fix: Evaluate the audit under genuinely concurrent request execution and continuous batching, with varied prefix lengths/page boundaries, cancellation/eviction, multiple documents, and at least another hybrid runtime/model family.
issues.verification_test: For each expanded setting, show that clean independent controls preserve registered semantics and that relevant live aliasing, stale-lease, tail, and dispatch faults reach predeclared gates without introducing false positives.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-setting receipt/replay summaries, fault outcomes, process-level memory measurements, and a protocol that reports failures rather than only successful configurations.

issues.location: Sections 5.3-5.5, pp. 8-9; Table 19, p. 22; Appendix I, p. 23
issues.observed_evidence: Cross-cell equality is explicitly relational. The independent attention check covers eight preselected rows conditional on captured post-RoPE inputs, while the GDN oracle covers four layers and four tokens after native q/k normalization. Dispatch provenance remains partial because no per-call compiled-binary or autotuning binding is captured (Table 5, p. 15).
issues.why_it_matters: Matching all registered cells does not exclude shared semantic, upstream-activation, fused-kernel, or compilation-path defects. The small selected sidecars reduce this risk only locally, so they do not establish correctness of the hybrid stack whose state ownership is being audited.
issues.required_fix: Add an end-to-end small-instance reference across all hybrid layers and broaden numerical/operator checks across layers, positions, query windows, and compiled paths. Bind actual kernel/binary selection per call where feasible.
issues.verification_test: Compare complete token/logit/state trajectories against an independently implemented, small-scale reference across multiple randomized prefixes and fan-outs, while demonstrating that intentionally wrong kernels or dispatch selections are detected.
issues.evidence_needed: Full-layer reference comparisons, dispatch/binary provenance traces, expanded oracle coverage, and predeclared error thresholds with both clean and faulted results.

issues.observed_evidence: The reproducibility statement reports extensive manifests and one-command replays, but the PDF supplies only relative artifact paths and says most full tensors require the pinned model/data environment for independent numerical recomputation. The submission itself does not show artifact availability, exact environment creation, or enough raw records to independently check the claimed replay results.
issues.why_it_matters: A reader of the paper cannot determine whether the reported replay boundary is executable and complete, which is especially consequential because the paper's contribution is an auditable receipt package.
issues.required_fix: Provide a stable anonymous artifact link, exact environment/container specification, expected runtime and hardware requirements, a minimal replay command, and a small self-contained raw example that exercises each principal predicate.
issues.verification_test: A clean-machine reproduction should execute the documented minimal replay and reproduce the listed aggregate decisions and deliberate-fault outcomes without manual reconstruction.
issues.evidence_needed: Anonymous artifact availability, pinned dependency/environment files, execution instructions, and complete expected-output hashes for a compact public test case.

llm_usage_disclosure: I am an LLM reviewer. This review used PDF-only access to the frozen submission; I did not inspect repositories, artifacts, prior reviews, or external sources.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: Independent producer recapture or a separately implemented execution/capture path confirming the central ownership predicates.
End-to-end independent validation across all hybrid layers and compiled dispatch paths, not only selected captured-input rows.
A multi-runtime/model and concurrent-serving evaluation with predeclared fault campaigns and transparent failures.
A complete anonymous, executable artifact that permits third-party replay of both clean and faulted cases.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Failure of independent capture or end-to-end references to agree with the receipt conclusions.
Evidence that any clean configuration aliases mutable request state, mutates document/base state, or changes registered semantics across ownership cells.
Discovery that selected oracle rows, mutation gates, or reported allocator endpoints cannot be reproduced from the documented package.
Citation or provenance checks showing that the reported related-work/context values or official-code claims are materially inaccurate.
review_limitations: This assessment is limited to the supplied PDF. I could assess internal consistency and visible citation coverage, but not independently verify artifacts, execution, or external reference accuracy.
